summary: Gov. Kevin Stitt (Republican) was term-limited, so the seat was open. Mike Mazzei (Republican) won, defeating Cyndi Munson (Democrat) and three independents.

candidates.name: Mike Mazzei
candidates.bio: Mike Mazzei is a financial planner who served in the Oklahoma Senate from 2004 to 2016 and as Gov. Kevin Stitt's secretary of budget. He won the 2026 Republican nomination for governor in a runoff.

positions.summary: Says he would make Oklahoma a no-income-tax state and eliminate property tax for seniors and veterans.
Says he would prioritize third-grade reading proficiency, more parental transparency, and teacher pay that is "tops in the region."
Says he would end special tax breaks for green energy and stop the Land Office from selling state land for green energy projects.
His campaign says he "opposes abortion in all circumstances."

candidates.name: Cyndi Munson
candidates.bio: Cyndi Munson is a member of the Oklahoma House of Representatives and its Democratic minority leader. She won the 2026 Democratic nomination for governor.

positions.summary: Says funding public education is her top priority.
Opposes across-the-board income tax cuts, says she would offer tax relief, and plans to work with the legislature to raise the state minimum wage.
Says she would protect Medicaid expansion and help small rural hospitals receive federal rural health funding.
Says she will support a state question to overturn Oklahoma's abortion ban.
Says she would pause new data center projects by executive order and opposes the proposed Inola smelter over environmental concerns.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (MultiState governors tracker, updated Nov 4, 35 of 36 races called). Summary note moved: results were unofficial.
